name: JDK, JRE, and JVM
overview: Three acronyms, three jobs. Follow a class from compilation to execution and explain where its objects and method calls live.

sections.title: Separate tools from runtime
sections.content: The JDK includes tools such as javac and a Java runtime. The runtime supplies the JVM and libraries. The JVM executes bytecode.

images.caption: The development kit supplies tools and a runtime. The JVM executes bytecode.

sections.title: Follow class startup
sections.content: The JVM loads, links, and initializes classes. Linking includes verification. Class initialization runs static field initializers and static blocks when applicable.

sections.title: Place state and work
sections.content: Objects live on the shared heap. Each thread keeps method frames on its own stack. The interpreter and JIT execute code, and the garbage collector reclaims unreachable objects.

keyPoints: Sketch one method call. Put its frame on the thread's stack and its new object on the shared heap. Now you can explain the difference without reciting a table.

references.title: Oracle JVM Specification - Official JVM architecture documentation

interviewQA.question: Which component compiles source?
interviewQA.answer: javac is a JDK tool. The JVM runs the compiled bytecode.

interviewQA.question: Where does a method call keep its local variables?
interviewQA.answer: The call has a frame on the executing thread’s stack. A local reference can point to an object on the heap.
